'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Tigray War]]
**According to a [[United Nations]] spokesperson, at least 16 UN staff and dependents have been detained in [[Addis Ababa]]. The [[Ethiopian Human Rights Commission]] also said that it had received many reports of arrests of [[Tigrayans]] in the city, including elders and mothers with children. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/un-says-least-nine-staff-dependents-detained-ethiopia-2021-11-09/ (Reuters)]
**The [[United Kingdom]] urges its [[Citizenship|citizens]] to leave [[Ethiopia]] and warns against all travel to the country amid fears that rebel forces will attack Addis Ababa and overthrow the [[Abiy Ahmed]] [[government of Ethiopia|government]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-59227117 (BBC News)]
*[[2021 Tunisian political crisis]]
**A man is killed as police in the town of Aguereb, [[Sfax Governorate]], [[Tunisia]], use [[tear gas]] against a protest outside a hospital where injured protesters are recovering. A police station is also [[Arson|set on fire]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/9/tunisian-police-fire-tear-gas-on-protesters-at-landfill (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**Security forces in [[Togo]] repel an attack at a security outpost in [[Kpendjal Prefecture]] in the far north of the country, pushing back the attackers to [[Burkina Faso]]. It is the first [[Islamic extremism|Islamist]] incident in Togo. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/togo-says-repelled-possible-militant-attack-near-burkina-faso-border-2021-11-13/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Freetown fuel tanker explosion]]
**The death toll from the [[fuel tank]]er explosion in [[Freetown]], [[Sierra Leone]], which occurred four days ago, increases to 115. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-59205372 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in England]]
*****[[Secretary of State for Health and Social Care|Health Secretary]] [[Sajid Javid]] announces that frontline [[NHS]] workers in [[England]] will be required to be vaccinated beginning in April 2022 in order to keep their jobs or risk being [[dismissal (employment)|fired]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-mandatory-jabs-will-be-introduced-for-nhs-englands-1-2-million-full-time-staff-from-april-sajid-javid-says-12464665 (Sky News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria]]
****[[Bulgaria]] reports a record 334 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 25,408. [https://bnr.bg/en/post/101553818/record-number-of-daily-coronavirus-deaths-in-bulgaria (Radio Bulgaria)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[President of France|President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] announces that beginning from December 15, people aged above 65 years old will be required to receive the [[booster dose]] of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] in order to maintain their [[Vaccine passports during the COVID-19 pandemic|Health Pass]]. He also announces that people aged 50 to 64 years old will become eligible for the booster dose from early December. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/11/09/frances-macron-extends-booster-shots-says-will-be-required-for-health-pass-.html (CNBC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 8,613 new casea of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 801,208. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/greece-breaks-new-record-on-daily-coronavirus-infections/2416420 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 1,211 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours after lifting workplace shutdowns, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 249,215. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/11/09/russia-marks-new-covid-death-toll-after-lifting-partial-lockdown-a75512 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record 833 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 73,390. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-europe-ukraine-coronavirus-vaccine-health-71734f0a649be270b76564dd27009702 (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Canada]]
***[[Health Canada]] authorizes the use of booster doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] for people over the age of 18. [https://globalnews.ca/news/8360613/pfizer-booster-dose-health-canada-covid19-vaccine/ (Global News)]
*[[China]] reports an outbreak of [[African swine fever]] at a pig farm that contains 1,063 animals in the island province of [[Hainan]]. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-11-09/china-reports-african-swine-fever-outbreak-on-hainan-island-oie-says (U.S. News and World Report)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2021 Belarus–European Union border crisis]], [[Poland–Russia relations]]
**[[Prime Minister of Poland|Polish Prime Minister]] [[Mateusz Morawiecki]] blames [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] for orchestrating the migrant crisis on the [[Belarus–Poland border]], saying that the crisis "has its mastermind in [[Moscow]]". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-59226226 (BBC News)]
**[[Lithuania]] announces a [[state of emergency]] for the first time since its independence as neighbouring Poland sees attacks on its border. [https://www.lrt.lt/en/news-in-english/19/1537044/lithuania-declares-state-of-emergency-on-border-with-belarus LRT]
*[[Syria–United Arab Emirates relations]]
**[[United Arab Emirates|Emirati]] Foreign Minister [[Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan]] meets with [[President of Syria|Syrian President]] [[Bashar al-Assad]], for the first time since the outbreak of the [[Syrian Civil War]] ten years ago, to discuss "ways to develop cooperation in different sectors that are of common interest". [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20211109-uae-top-diplomat-on-first-syria-visit-in-over-a-decade (France 24)]
*[[Audrey Azoulay]] is re-elected for a second term as the Director-General of [[UNESCO]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/frances-azoulay-re-elected-to-head-unesco-as-it-seeks-to-woo-back-israel-us/ (AFP via ''The Times of Israel'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Capital punishment in Singapore]]
**[[Human rights]] organizations urge [[Singapore]] to cancel the [[execution]] of a 33-year-old [[Malaysians in Singapore|Malaysian]] [[Intellectual disability|mentally impaired]] man who was [[criminal conviction|convicted]] after being caught in 2010 with 42.72 grams of [[heroin]]. The court had postponed an initial execution date scheduled for last week and was expected to hang the man today. However, the court postponed the execution again after the man was diagnosed with COVID-19. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/9/singapore-urged-to-halt-execution-of-mentally-impaired-man (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Pandora Papers]]
**The process of [[impeachment]] against [[Chile]]an [[President of Chile|President]] [[Sebastián Piñera]] moves to the [[Senate of Chile|Senate]] after passing the [[Chamber of Deputies of Chile|lower-chamber]] overnight. In order to remove Piñera from power, the impeachment will need to pass the Senate with a two-thirds vote. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/chile-impeachment-vote-heads-senate-after-lower-house-approval-2021-11-09/ (Reuters)]
*A man threatens passers-by with a knife in [[Bislett]], [[Oslo]], [[Norway]], before being shot dead by police. The motive behind the perpetrator's act is currently unknown, but is under investigation. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/man-with-knife-attacks-passers-by-in-norway-is-shot-dead/2021/11/09/fda955c4-414b-11ec-9404-50a28a88b9cd_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
